title: Per-tenant rolling soft-guard and soft-throttle controller for reserved capacity pools
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a per-tenant rolling "soft-guard" mechanism layered on top of existing reserved-capacity quotas. The soft-guard smooths abrupt resets and prevents short-term burst amplification when many tenants renew monthly/daily windows or when reserved pools experience correlated resets across timezones. It provides a temporary, decaying allowance that allows short bursts but gradually enforces hard limits to protect shared reserved pools and downstream billing correctness.
background: We repeatedly observe brief but intense bursts at quota reset boundaries (midnight UTC, month starts) and when customers switch from hosted to reserved capacity. These spikes cause token-level overcommit, billing reconciliation churn, and unfair immediate preemption of lower-priority tenants. Existing rolling-window and epoch-based solutions reduce some effects, but we still see correlated renewals create transient overuse in the reserved pool and interfere with autoscaler behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant soft-guard implemented in quota service and enabled behind feature flag
Soft-guard algorithm exposes configuration: decay half-life, allowance multiplier, max temporary overage
Integration tests cover timezone-shifted resets, tenant churn, and reserved-pool contention scenarios
Telemetry: per-tenant temporary allowance usage, spikes avoided, and occurrences reported to Console
Rollback path: feature flag off reverts to current quota semantics without data loss
No measurable increase (>5%) in request latency at the quota-check path under typical load
proposal: Add a decaying-buffer per tenant that primes when a tenant's quota window renews or when the tenant returns from idle. The buffer acts as an additive allowance that decays exponentially with a configurable half-life (default: 30 minutes). Behavior details:
proposal_points: Buffer initialization: at window reset the tenant receives a temporary allowance = min(configured_multiplier * nominal_quota, configured_max_overage).
Consumption order: requests first consume cached prefix/KV, then soft-guard allowance, then hard quota. If soft-guard is exhausted, standard throttling applies.
Decay model: exponential decay applied server-side with periodic checkpointing. Decay computed deterministically using last-checkpoint timestamp to avoid per-token updates.

Fairness: when reserved pool contention is detected (pool utilization > configured threshold), a proportional scaling factor reduces all tenant soft-allowances to preserve SLAs and headroom for control-plane ops.

Billing alignment: any consumption covered by soft-guard is recorded with special markers so billing reconciliation can treat it as regular usage (no free credit), but can be flagged for post-hoc smoothing if tenant is on reserved contract with proration rules.
Config surface: tenant-level flags (enabled/disabled), multiplier, max_overage, half_life, pool_shedding_threshold, and emergency_kill-switch for operators.
Persistence: keep allowance and last-update timestamps in the quota-store (existing Redis+raft snapshot model) with compacted checkpoints; do not create unbounded growth per-tenant.
Backwards-compatible: default values set conservatively so behaviour is opt-in for early customers and escalated later for tenants with recurring burst patterns.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Feature flag gated rollout to internal reserved accounts (2 weeks): collect telemetry and validate no degradation
Phase 2 - Beta for small set of paying customers with engineering support (4 weeks): iterate on config defaults
Phase 3 - Gradual opt-in for all reserved customers with targeted recommendations from Optimize (8 weeks)
Emergency rollback: flip feature flag off at control plane; quota-store snapshots are preserved and expected to be ignored by legacy path
telemetry_and_metrics: Billing consistency: reconciliation_delta_count where temporary allowance led to post-facto adjustments
testing_plan: Unit tests for decay math and deterministic checkpointing
Integration test harness that simulates N tenants resetting across a 24h window with timezone offsets
Chaos test: simulate quota-store leader failover during heavy decay updates
Load test: ensure quota-check path latencies stay within SLO under QPS of 5x production for reserved pool
Billing regression tests to ensure soft-guard markers do not alter invoiced totals unintentionally
implementation_tasks: Schema changes in quota-store: add allowance and last_checkpoint_ts fields (compact nanosecond integer values)
Quota service: compute deterministic decay on read + checkpoint on write; expose admin endpoints for inspection
Rate-limiter integration: consume soft-allowance atomically with existing token deduct path
Router: include soft-guard flag in routing decisions for preemption/fallback policies
Console: add per-tenant soft-guard panel and alert when shedding occurs
Billing: add marker to usage events and update reconciliation scripts to accommodate optional smoothing rules
Docs: SDK/Policy docs describing semantics, config options, and recommended defaults
open_questions: What default half-life balances smoothing vs. predictability for 95th percentile workloads?
Should consumption that uses soft-guard be billed immediately or delayed until end-of-window for tenants with reserved contracts?
Is exponential decay sufficient or do we need workload-adaptive decay (shorter half-life for chat workloads)?
How do we ensure accurate telemetry when tenants rapidly toggle the feature?
Does the persistent footprint of soft-guard state require sharding changes to quota-store?
